form.notes: NOT read. The agency's own site (ecmc.colorado.gov) answers 403 to a plain automated request and 200 to one that names itself; that was used for its downloads page only. sources.tested: Read 2026-11-01 with a plain automated agent: 200 from every host the producer uses. Layer metadata: 124,468 rows, maxRecordCount 2,000, rebuilt daily. A count query and four pages of 2,000 by OBJECTID give the 6,500 wells spud since 2019 (6 requests, 3 s apart, about 1.3 MB, 18 s). spud_date is described as the 'best spud date available'. The class is set when the completion is reported (of the last year's 667 new wells 183 are oil, 10 gas and 474 not yet classed). The older ECMC_Wells service address returns 404.

sources.tested: Layer metadata read 2026-11-01 (28 attribute fields plus the shape; the Permits shapefile PERMITS_SHP.ZIP of the downloads page is the same content, its metadata record dated 2018 lists Perm_Type, Perm_Appr, Perm_Exp and Prop_Depth). grade_reason: The Commission's Wells (API Spots) map layer is free, needs no login, is rebuilt daily and has one row per well since 1999 with a spud date, a well class, county, operator and location; the Permits layer holds open permits with a received date, expiry date, type and proposed depth. No file carries the day a permit was approved: the approved-permits search lists it for the last 12 months only, behind a form with no export. So Colorado is read by spud date (B, never added to permits), and its well class is set only when the completion is filed. Updated 2026-11-01: the two layers and the Commission's own yearly well-starts table were read by a script; the 403s the first research met were the agency's main site, which answers a request that names itself.
producer_plan: Built: d11_nat_co.py (measure spuds). Reads the Wells layer (Wells_Public_ECMC, layer 0) for spud_date from 2019 on: a count query, then pages of 2,000 by OBJECTID (6 requests, 3 s apart, about 18 s), asking only spud_date, County, well_class, Operator and facility_id (to see a well's second row). A well counts once, on its first spud date; the last 30 days are left off. Bands: OW, GW, CBM, DA, LO or a blank class = new (71% have no class yet, so fluid is unknown, never oil by default); DSPW, the two EPA classes, ERIW, STOW = inj; helium, CO2, domestic, observation, stratigraphic and other codes = other; redrill, rework and amend are null. Each run is checked against the Commission's Annual Well Starts by County table (the last three full years within 10%). Fails on an error reply, a missing field, under 4,000 rows, bad dates over 1%, unknown classes over 3%, a newest spud over 30 days old. A permits series would need the 12-month approved-permits search read weekly and kept (24 months by November 2027); not built.
privacy_notes: The layers hold operator numbers, company names and well names; the producer asks for five fields only (spud date, county, class, operator, facility number) and names an operator only if it is a corporation, LLC or partnership. The download page names GIS staff contacts (not copied). Form 2 was not read, so whether it asks for surface or mineral owner details is unknown.
